hints.title: Identifying Non-Purchasing Visits
hints.text: A customer visit results in no transaction if there is no corresponding row in Transactions matching visit_id.

hints.title: Left Outer Join with Null Check
hints.text: left join Visits with Transactions on visit_id. filter rows where transaction_id is null.

hints.title: Grouping by Customer ID
hints.text: group by customer_id and count matching visits as count_no_trans.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT v.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS count_no_trans
FROM Visits v
LEFT JOIN Transactions t ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id
WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL
GROUP BY v.customer_id;
```

complexity.notes: Executes hash anti-join between visits and transactions followed by grouping on customer_id.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated not exists subquery runs in quadratic time without appropriate index support.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hash left join with null predicate identifies unmatched visits in linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Standard anti-join pattern using left outer join with null check or not in.

import pandas as pd

def find_customers(visits: pd.DataFrame, transactions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = visits.merge(transactions, on='visit_id', how='left')
    no_trans = merged[merged['transaction_id'].isna()]
    res = no_trans.groupby('customer_id').size().reset_index(name='count_no_trans')
    return res
solutions.approach: Pandas Left Merge with Isna Filter
